hints.title: Track Server Release Times
hints.text: Maintain busy servers with their completion times to free them as requests arrive.

hints.title: Maintain Available Server IDs
hints.text: Maintain available server IDs in a structure allowing fast lookup for the next available ID >= i % k.

hints.title: Wrap Around Search
hints.text: If no server with ID >= i % k is available, wrap around to find the smallest available server ID.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq
import bisect

class Solution:
    def busiestServers(self, k: int, arrival: list[int], load: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        busy = []  # (end_time, server_id)
        avail = list(range(k))
        count = [0] * k
        for i, (t, l) in enumerate(zip(arrival, load)):
            while busy and busy[0][0] <= t:
                _, s = heapq.heappop(busy)
                bisect.insort(avail, s)
            if not avail:
                continue
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(avail, i % k)
            if idx == len(avail):
                idx = 0
            server = avail.pop(idx)
            count[server] += 1
            heapq.heappush(busy, (t + l, server))
        max_c = max(count)
        return [i for i, c in enumerate(count) if c == max_c]
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all k servers sequentially for each request results in O(n * k) time, which times out for n, k = 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Min-heaps and ordered sets allow logarithmic time server assignment and release.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle the modulo wrap-around logic cleanly with logarithmic search.

solutions.approach: Min-heap for busy servers and bisect on available list
